In this experiment, you will look at the operation of a heat valve associated with a thermostat in an aircraft air conditioning system.
EXPERIMENT
From comparing the actual and desired temperature, the thermostat circuit sends an open or closed signal to the motor circuitry which will open or close the heat valve.
When the room is too hot, a signal is present on the HOT ROOM test point, causing the heat valve to close. This allows the room to cool to an ambient temperature.
The PC130-733 card is the heat valve controller circuit. Pick it up and examine it.
The direction the motor turns depends on the signal received from the thermostat circuits. Remember, these are the COLD ROOM and HOT ROOM signals.
When the block closes the top switch, it indicates to the control circuit that the heat valve is completely closed and to stop the motor from turning.
The switches are performing two functions: they provide feedback on the current valve position, and they protect the motor from becoming damaged once the valve reaches a maximum position...
